section.content: 本发明涉及半导体装置和半导体集成电路。提供一种半导体装置，能够迅速稳定用于控制电流源的控制电压。半导体装置包括滤波器电路，该滤波器电路被设置在控制电压产生电路与电流源之间，并且去除控制电压的噪声。所述滤波器电路包括：第一电阻元件，其被设置在控制电压产生电路与输出控制电压的输出节点之间；第一电容元件，其被设置在输出节点与第一电压之间；第二电容元件，其经由第一开关元件来被耦合在输出节点与第一电压之间。当第一开关元件为非导通时，第二电容元件被耦合在第一电压与第二电压之间。当第一开关元件为导通时，第二电容元件通过输出节点来与第一电容元件耦合。

The present invention relates to a semiconductor device and a semiconductor integrated circuit. Provided is a semiconductor device capable of quickly stabilizing a control voltage for controlling a current source. The semiconductor device includes a filter circuit that is provided between the control voltage generation circuit and the current source and removes noise of the control voltage. The filter circuit includes: a first resistance element provided between the control voltage generation circuit and an output node that outputs the control voltage; a first capacitive element provided between the output node and a first voltage; a second capacitive element coupled between the output node and the first voltage via the first switching element. The second capacitive element is coupled between the first voltage and the second voltage when the first switching element is non-conductive. When the first switch element is on, the second capacitive element is coupled to the first capacitive element through the output node.

Semiconductor device and semiconductor integrated circuitCross Reference to Related Applications

The disclosure of Japanese patent application No.2015-247356, filed 12/18/2015, including the specification, drawings and abstract, is hereby incorporated by reference in its entirety.

Technical Field

The present disclosure relates to a semiconductor device and a semiconductor integrated circuit having a filter circuit.

Background

In the related art, low power consumption and high-speed performance are highly demanded for general-purpose memories such as flash memories in terms of semiconductor integrated circuits.

In general, a flash memory or the like is provided with various modes to meet low power consumption requirements. For example, a method is adopted in which a low power consumption mode is provided and the power supply circuit is stopped.

Further, in order to satisfy high-speed performance, it is necessary to quickly stabilize a voltage output from a power supply circuit included in a flash memory, for example.

In this regard, japanese unexamined patent application publication No.2001-319488 proposes a method of stabilizing the bias voltage output from the bias circuit to ensure high-speed performance of the read system circuit.

Disclosure of Invention

On the other hand, it is known that feedback noise from the entire semiconductor integrated circuit occurs in the bias voltage output from the bias circuit, and as a countermeasure against this problem, a configuration is adopted in which a filter circuit that removes noise is provided to a power supply circuit (e.g., bias circuit).

However, there is a problem that it takes time for the voltage level output from the power supply circuit to stabilize to a desired voltage level due to the influence of the capacitance component of the filter circuit.

Other objects and novel features will become apparent from the description of the specification and drawings.

According to an embodiment, a semiconductor device includes: a current source; a control voltage generation circuit that outputs a control voltage for controlling the current source; and a filter circuit which is provided between the control voltage generation circuit and the current source and removes noise of the control voltage. The filter circuit includes: a first resistance element provided between the control voltage generation circuit and an output node that outputs the control voltage; a first capacitive element provided between the output node and a first voltage; a second capacitive element coupled in parallel with the first capacitive element between the output node and the first voltage; a first switching element disposed between the second capacitive element and the output node. The second capacitive element is coupled between the first voltage and the second voltage when the first switching element is non-conductive. When the first switching element is turned on, the second capacitive element is coupled with the first capacitive element through the output node.

According to the embodiment, the control voltage for controlling the current source can be rapidly stabilized.

Detailed Description

The embodiments are described in detail below with reference to the accompanying drawings. In the drawings, the same or corresponding parts are denoted by the same reference numerals, and the description thereof will not be repeated.

A. Integral arrangement

Fig. 1 is a schematic diagram of an overall configuration of a semiconductor integrated circuit according to an embodiment.

As shown in fig. 1, in this example, a single-chip microcomputer (also referred to as a data processor or a microprocessor) will be described as an example of the semiconductor integrated circuit 1. Although not particularly limited, the microcomputer is formed on one semiconductor substrate (chip) such as single crystal silicon by a known semiconductor integrated circuit manufacturing technique.

The semiconductor integrated circuit 1 includes a memory module having a flash memory.

The semiconductor integrated circuit 1 includes an internal bus 2, a CPU (central processing unit) 3, a RAM (random access memory) 4, a bus controller 5, an oscillator 6, a frequency dividing circuit 7, a memory module 8, a power supply circuit 9, an input/output port (I/O)10, and a peripheral circuit 11.

The peripheral circuit 11 includes an AD converter and a timing counter.

The internal bus 2 includes an address bus, a data bus, and a control bus.

The circuit modules are coupled to each other through an internal bus 2 and perform data transmission/reception.

The CPU3 controls the entire semiconductor integrated circuit 1. The CPU3 includes an instruction control unit and an execution unit. The CPU3 decodes the acquired instruction and executes arithmetic processing in the execution unit according to the decoding result.

The RAM 4 is used as a work area of the CPU 2 and the like.

The bus controller 5 performs arbitration control of the internal bus 2, and controls data transmission/reception using the internal bus 2. Specifically, the bus controller 5 responds to an access request from the CPU3, and performs arbitration control of the number of access cycles, the number of wait states, the bus width, and the like, according to the target address of the access.

The oscillator 6 generates a clock signal. The oscillator 6 is coupled to a frequency dividing circuit 7, and generates and outputs an operation reference clock signal and other internal clock signals for controlling various circuits by dividing the frequency of the clock signal.

The memory module 8 has a flash memory (as an example), and stores an operation program, data, and the like of the CPU 3.

The power supply circuit 9 generates voltages of various circuit blocks.

The CPU3 performs erase and write control on the memory module 8.

In a device test stage or a manufacturing stage, an external write device (not shown in the drawings) can directly perform erase and write control on the memory module 8 through the input/output port 10.

After power-on, the inside of the semiconductor integrated circuit 1 is initialized during the low level of the reset signal. When the reset is released by the high level of the reset signal, the CPU3 starts execution of the program in the program area designated by the vector in address 0 or the like.

Fig. 2 is a schematic diagram for explaining a configuration of the memory module 8 according to the embodiment.

As shown in FIG. 2, memory module 8 includes input/output circuitry 21, control circuitry 22, address buffer 23, power supply circuitry 24, pre-decoder 25, row decoder/driver 26, write latch 27, sense amplifier circuitry 28, column decoder 29, memory array 30, source decoder/driver 31, and current source 32.

The memory array 30 includes a plurality of flash memories arranged in a matrix form.

The input/output circuit 21 is coupled to the external internal bus 2, and transmits and receives data and commands.

The control circuit 22 controls each circuit in the memory module 8.

An address buffer 23 is coupled to the external internal bus 2 and holds addresses for accessing the memory array 30.

The power supply circuit 24 supplies necessary voltages to each circuit in the memory module 8. Specifically, the power supply circuit 24 generates voltages for writing and erasing, and generates a voltage for driving the current source 32.

The pre-decoder 25 pre-decodes the address to be used to access the memory array 30.

Row decoder/driver 26 decodes row address X from address buffer 23 and drives the word lines.

Write latch 27 is coupled to current source 32 and holds the data to be written to memory array 30.

The sense amplifier circuit 28 amplifies a signal read from the memory array 30 during data reading and outputs the signal as read data.

The column decoder 29 decodes a column address Y from the address buffer 23 and selects a bit line and the like.

The source decoder/driver 31 drives the source line.

Fig. 3 is a schematic diagram for explaining transition of modes of the memory module 8 according to the embodiment.

As shown in fig. 3, here is shown a case where the mode is changed from the standby mode to the read standby mode and the mode is changed from the read standby mode to the read mode or the write/erase mode.

The standby mode is a low power consumption mode. In the standby mode, the power supply circuit 24 and the current source 32 inside the memory module 8 are set to an inactive mode. As an example, the return operation from the low power consumption mode is performed in accordance with the input of the standby signal STBYP ("L" level) input from the CPU 3. In the present example, the mode is changed from the standby mode to the read standby mode. Thus, power supply circuit 24 and current source 32 inside memory module 8 are set to an active mode.

Then, the mode is changed from the read standby mode to the read mode, and data reading is performed.

On the other hand, the mode is changed from the read standby mode to the standby mode (which is a low power consumption mode) according to the input of the standby signal STBYP ("H" level) input from the CPU 3.

Fig. 4 is a schematic diagram for explaining transition of the standby mode and the read standby mode of the memory module 8 according to the embodiment.

As shown in fig. 4, a case is shown in which the mode of the memory module 8 is changed in accordance with the standby signal STBYP input from the CPU 3. Specifically, a case is shown in which the read standby mode is set when the standby signal STBYP is at the "L" level. When the standby signal STBYP transitions to the "H" level at time T1, the mode transitions from the read standby mode to the standby mode.

Next, when the standby signal STBYP transitions to the "L" level at time T2, the mode transitions from the standby mode to the read standby mode.

On the other hand, when the mode is changed from the standby mode to the read standby mode, the power supply circuit 24 and the current source 32 inside the memory module 8 are set to the activated mode, thereby providing a predetermined waiting state until the voltage from the power supply circuit 24 and the current from the current source 32 are stabilized. In the present example, after waiting for one waiting time tW ═ P μ s, the mode transitions to the read standby mode at time T3.

Fig. 5 is a schematic diagram for explaining data reading according to the embodiment.

As shown in fig. 5, in the read standby mode, the mode is shifted to the read mode in accordance with a chip enable signal CE included in an instruction from the CPU3 to read data from the memory module 8.

As an example, at time T4, the mode is changed from the read standby mode to the read mode according to the "L level" of the chip enable signal CE.

Then, the memory block 8 operates in synchronization with the internal clock signal CLK generated by the frequency dividing circuit 7.

When the internal clock signal CLK rises from "L level" to "H level", the external address signal AD inputted from the outside is latched by the address buffer 23 of the memory module 8.

The latched external address signal AD is output as an X address and a Y address to the pre-decoder 25 and the column decoder 29, respectively. Then, the signal pre-decoded by the pre-decoder 25 is input to a row decoder/driver 26. Then, the row decoder/driver 26 performs row selection based on the X address. In addition, the column decoder 29 decodes the Y address and performs column selection. Thus, a designated memory cell in the memory array 30 is accessed and data is read from the memory cell.

Then, the read data DOUT that has been read is output to the internal bus 2 through the input/output circuit 21.

In the present example, a case is shown in which data is read twice according to input of the external address signal AD in the read mode.

At time T5, the mode transitions from the read mode to the read standby mode according to the "H level" of the chip enable signal CE.

Fig. 6 is a schematic diagram for explaining a configuration of a part of the power supply circuit 24 according to the embodiment.

As shown in fig. 6, the power supply circuit 24 includes a control voltage generation circuit and a filter circuit 55 having charge sharing.

A filter circuit 55 having charge sharing is provided between the control voltage generation circuit and the current source 32, and removes noise of the control voltage. In the present example, a low pass filter circuit including a resistive element and a capacitive element is provided. The cutoff frequency of the filter circuit is set based on the resistance component of the resistance element and the capacitance component of the capacitance element.

A filter circuit with charge sharing 55 described later is provided with a circuit that can share electric charge. The circuit that can share the charge operates according to the activation signal EAMP.

The control voltage generation circuit outputs a control voltage for controlling the current source.

The control voltage generating circuit includes an operational Amplifier (AMP)50, a P-channel MOS transistor MOS1, and resistance elements R1 and R2.

The source of P-channel MOS transistor MOS1 is coupled to supply voltage VCC, and the drain is coupled to resistive element R1. The gate of the P-channel MOS transistor MOS1 receives the output signal of AMP 50.

The AMP 50 is activated in response to the activation signal EAMP. In this example, AMP 50 is activated in accordance with activation signal EAMP ("H" level), and AMP 50 is deactivated in accordance with activation signal EAMP ("L" level).

In the standby mode, the activation signal EAMP is set to the "L" level. In the read standby mode, the activation signal EAMP is set to an "H" level.

The coupled node of resistive elements R1 and R2 is fed back to AMP 50 and coupled to one of the input terminals.

The other input terminal of the AMP 50 receives an input of the reference voltage Vref. The AMP 50 regulates the voltage output to the P-channel MOS transistor MOS1 so that the voltage of the coupling node of the resistance elements R1 and R2 is the same as the reference voltage Vref.

The filter circuit 55 with charge sharing is coupled to the output of the AMP 50, removes a noise component of the control voltage output from the AMP 50, and then outputs the control voltage to the current source 32.

The current source 32 receives the control voltage output from the AMP 50, and is adjusted so that the same current as that flowing through the resistance elements R1 and R2 flows.

Fig. 7 is a schematic diagram for explaining a configuration of the filter circuit with charge sharing 55 according to the embodiment.

As shown in fig. 7, the filter circuit with charge sharing 55 includes a resistance element R, capacitance elements C1 and C2, and switching elements SW1 and SW 2. The capacitance elements C1 and C2 and the switching elements SW1 and SW2 form a charge sharing circuit.

The switching element SW1 includes a transmission gate. Specifically, the switching element SW1 includes an N-channel MOS transistor and a P-channel MOS transistor coupled in parallel with each other. The activation signal EAMP is input to the gate of the N-channel MOS transistor. The inverted signal/EAMP of the activation signal EAMP is input to the gate of the P-channel MOS transistor. The switching element SW2 includes an N-channel MOS transistor. The inverted signal/EAMP of the activation signal EAMP is input to the gate of the N-channel MOS transistor.

The resistance element R is provided between the control voltage generation circuit and the output node N1.

The capacitive element C1 is disposed between the output node N1 and the power supply voltage VCC.

The capacitive element C2 is coupled between the output node N1 and the supply voltage VCC through a switching element SW1 in parallel with the capacitive element C1.

Capacitive element C2 is coupled between supply voltage VCC and internal node N2.

The switching element SW1 is disposed between the output node N1 and the internal node N2, and is set to a conductive/non-conductive state (ON/OFF) according to the activation signal EAMP.

The switching element SW2 is disposed between the internal node N2 and the ground voltage VSS, and is set to a conductive/non-conductive state (ON/OFF) according to the inverted signal/EAMP of the activation signal EAMP.

The switching element SW2 complementarily operates with the switching element SW1 according to the inverted signal/EAMP of the activation signal EAMP. When the switching element SW1 is in a conductive state, the switching element SW2 is in a non-conductive state, and when the switching element SW1 is in a non-conductive state, the switching element SW2 is in a conductive state.

In the standby mode, the activation signal EAMP is set to the "L" level. In this case, the output of the AMP 50 is set to the "H" level, so that the P-channel MOS transistor MOS1 is in a non-conductive state. Therefore, the current to the resistance elements R1 and R2 is turned off.

The filter circuit 55 with charge sharing is described below. According to the activation signal EAMP ("L" level), the switching element SW1 becomes a non-conductive state, and the switching element SW2 becomes a conductive state. Accordingly, the capacitive element C1 is charged to the power supply voltage VCC.

On the other hand, the switching element SW2 is in a conducting state, so that the capacitance element C2 is coupled to the ground voltage VSS and charged to the ground voltage VSS.

Then, in the read standby mode, the activation signal EAMP is set to an "H" level. In this case, the AMP 50 is activated and adjusts the voltage output to the P-channel MOS transistor MOS1 so that the voltage of the coupling node of the resistance elements R1 and R2 is the same as the reference voltage Vref.

Meanwhile, according to the activation signal EAMP ("H" level), the switching element SW1 becomes a conductive state, and the switching element SW2 becomes a non-conductive state. Thereby, the operation of the charge sharing circuit is started. The capacitive element C1 is coupled to C2, so that the charge of the capacitive element C1 charged to the power supply voltage VCC is shared by the capacitive element C2 charged to the ground voltage VSS through the switching element SW1 and charges the capacitive element C2.

After the voltage of the output node N1 and the voltage of the internal node N2 become the same, the control voltage output from the AMP 50 is adjusted so that the voltage of the coupling node of the resistance elements R1 and R2 becomes the same as the reference voltage Vref, and the control voltage is output to the current source 32 through the output node N1.

Fig. 8 is a schematic diagram for explaining a configuration of a part of a power supply circuit of a comparative example.

As shown in fig. 8, the configuration of the filter circuit of the power supply circuit is different from that shown in fig. 6. In the present example, a case is shown in which a filter circuit 51 (which is a normal low-pass filter circuit) is provided instead of the filter circuit 55 having charge sharing. The filter circuit 51 does not include a charge sharing circuit.

Fig. 9 is a schematic diagram for explaining generation of a control voltage of the control voltage generation circuit according to the activation signal AMP according to the embodiment.

As shown in fig. 9, in response to the activation signal EAMP rising from the "L" level to the "H" level, the AMP 50 is activated, and at the same time, the charge sharing circuit starts operating. Accordingly, the output node N1 is electrically coupled with the internal node N2 and is set to an intermediate voltage between the power supply voltage VCC and the ground voltage VSS. After the electric charge of the capacitive element C1 and the electric charge of the capacitive element C2 become the same, the control voltage output from the AMP 50 is adjusted so that the voltage of the coupling node of the resistive elements R1 and R2 becomes the same as the reference voltage Vref. Then, the control voltage is adjusted to the target voltage.

On the other hand, as shown in fig. 9, although the AMP 50 is activated in response to the activation signal EAMP rising from the "L" level to the "H" level also in the comparison circuit, the control voltage is gradually adjusted from the power supply voltage VCC to the target voltage by the capacitance component of the filter circuit 51.

Therefore, according to the present embodiment, by providing the filter circuit 55 with charge sharing, it is possible to quickly adjust the control voltage to the target voltage. Thereby, the waiting time tW described in fig. 4 can be significantly shortened, so that the mode can be quickly changed from the standby mode to the read standby mode.

Fig. 10 is a schematic diagram for explaining the relationship between the start-up time and the current consumption in the power supply circuit 24.

As shown in fig. 10, as the relationship between the startup time and the current consumption, it is necessary to increase the current consumption to shorten the startup time. That is, it is necessary to increase the operating voltage of the AMP 50 to increase the current consumption.

The filter circuit with charge sharing 55 according to the present embodiment adjusts the voltage by the charge movement of the charge sharing circuit, so that the control voltage can be quickly adjusted to the target voltage without increasing the current consumption.

When the switch SW1 is turned on, the capacitance elements C1 and C2 function as low-pass filter circuits.

The cutoff frequency of the filter circuit is set based on the capacitance elements C1 and C2 and the resistance element R1. Therefore, compared with the filter circuit 51 of the comparison circuit, it is not necessary to provide a redundant capacitance element, and only the switching elements SW1 and SW2 are added, so that enlargement of the circuit size can be suppressed.

In the present example, the switching element SW1 includes both a P-channel MOS transistor and an N-channel MOS transistor. However, the switching element SW1 may include any one of them.

In the present example, the configuration in which the capacitive elements C1 and C2 are coupled to the power supply voltage VCC is described as the configuration of a low-pass filter. However, in the case of a high-pass filter circuit or the like, the capacitance elements C1 and C2 may be coupled to the ground voltage VSS.

In the present example, a method is described in which high-speed startup can be performed in transition from the standby mode to the read standby mode. However, not limited to the above mode transition, for example, the method can be similarly applied to a case where the mode is changed from the standby mode to the read mode or the write/erase mode.

In the present example, the configuration of the power supply circuit used by the memory module 8 is described. However, without being limited to the memory module 8, the configuration may be similarly applied to a power supply circuit of another semiconductor device.

Although the present disclosure is specifically described based on the embodiment, the present disclosure is not limited to the embodiment and does not need to be illustrated, and various modifications may be made to the present disclosure without departing from the scope of the present disclosure.
